name: Back-face rasterized volume rendering
aliases: Backface Culling for Ray Casting Entry Points
Two-Pass Volume Ray Casting with Back-Face Coordinate Buffer
definition: A GPU implementation technique where the volume is rendered by rasterizing the back faces of its bounding box to trigger fragment shaders, which then perform raymarching. This avoids processing pixels outside the volume and handles zooming correctly.
summary: Back-face rasterized volume rendering is a GPU-accelerated technique that determines ray entry and exit points by rasterizing the volume's bounding box geometry, avoiding explicit ray-box intersection calculations.
